decision: held: the declared meta-analysis 30670267 (Complement Ther Med 2019) has no open full text; its abstract reports no dose, preparation or included trials, so it cannot be verified or excluded. The accessible systematic review 33827515 is completed as a non-credit context (GRADE low/very low). OA retry 2026-10-28: no open copy of 30670267 (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Europe PMC).
summary: 33827515 (5 RCTs) finds elderberry may not prevent colds and may shorten cold or influenza illness with uncertain evidence; it supports no credit and its oseltamivir comparison used a combination product, consistent with Dr. Pham's rejection of strong antiviral claims. 30670267 reports a large symptom effect in 180 participants but is abstract-only, so the record remains held.

identity.preparation: Proprietary elderberry extracts (capsule 300 mg, lozenge 175 mg, Sambucol syrup) and one echinacea-elderberry combination (Echinaforce Hotdrink)

population.description: Five randomized trials of prevention or treatment of viral respiratory illness (e.g., 312 air travellers in Tiralongo 2016; 87 participants across two Sambucol influenza trials; 420 in the oseltamivir comparison).

study_contexts.study_design: Systematic review with GRADE (Cochrane risk-of-bias tools); outcomes new illnesses, severity and duration; three ex vivo cytokine studies summarized separately.

outcomes.name: Common cold: may not reduce incidence; may reduce duration and severity, evidence uncertain
Influenza duration may be reduced versus placebo, very uncertain; echinacea-elderberry combination vs oseltamivir fewer recovered at day 1 (RR 0.36), little or no difference at days 5 and 10
No clinical inflammatory-outcome studies; ex vivo cytokine effects only

limitations: Small trials with incomplete outcome data and selection concerns; all estimates low or very low certainty. No pooled RCT estimate supports credit.
Dr. Pham's returned decision rejects strong antiviral and oseltamivir-equivalence claims; the oseltamivir comparison used an echinacea-elderberry combination.
Evidence uncertainty is a reviewed limitation, not proof of no biological activity.
